source_text: Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος παθεῖν καὶ ἀτιμασθῆναι ὑπέμεινε καὶ πάλιν μετὰ δόξης παραγενήσεται, ἀκούσατε τῶν εἰρημένων εἰς τοῦτο προφητειῶν. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Ἀνθ᾿ ὧν παρέδωκαν εἰς θάνατον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ τῶν ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη, αὐτὸς ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν εἴληφε καί τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐξιλάσεται. Ἴδε γὰρ συνήσει ὁ παῖς μου, καὶ ὑψωθήσεται καὶ δοξασθήσεται σφόδρα. Ὃν τρόπον ἐκστήσονται πολλοὶ ἐπὶ σέ, οὕτως ἀδοξήσει ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπων τὸ εἶδός σου καὶ ἡ δόξα σου ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οὕτως θαυμάσονται ἔθνη πολλά, καὶ συνέξουσι βασιλεῖς τὸ στόμα αἰτῶν· ὅτι οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται, καὶ οἳ οὐκ ἀκηκόασι συνήσουσι. Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσε τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη; Ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ὡς παιδίον, ὡς ῥίζα ἐν γῇ διψώσῃ. Οὐκ ἔστιν εἶδος αὐτῷ οὐδὲ δέξα· καὶ εἴδομεν αὐτόν, καὶ οὐκ εἶχεν εἶδος οὐδὲ κάλλος, ἀλλὰ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἄτιμον καὶ ἐκλεῖπον παρὰ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους. Ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὢν καὶ εἰδὼς φέρειν μαλακίαν, ὅτι ἀπέστραπται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, ἠτιμάσθη καὶ οὐκ ἐλογίσθη. Οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐλογισάμεθα αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν πόνῳ καὶ ἐν πληγῇ καὶ ἐν κακώσει. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν· παιδεία εἰρήνης ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, τῷ μώλωπι αἰτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν. Πάντες ὡς πρόβατα ἐπλανήθημεν, ἄνθρωπος τῇ ὁδῷ αὐτοῦ ἐπλανήθη· καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν ταῖς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ αὐτὸς διὰ τὸ κεκακῶσθαι οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη“. Μετὰ οἶν τὸ σταυρωθῆναι αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ γνώριμοι αὐτοῦ πάντες ἀπέστησαν, ἀρνησάμενοι αὐτόν· ὕστερον δέ, ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντος καὶ ὀφθέντος αὐτοῖς καὶ ταῖς προφητείαις ἐντυχεῖν, ἐν αἷς πάντα ταῦτα προείρητο γενησόμενα, διδάξαντος, καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες καὶ δύναμιν ἐκεῖθεν αἰτοῖς πεμφθεῖσαν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λαβόντες καὶ εἰς πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων ἐλθόντες, ταῦτα ἐδίδαξαν καὶ ἀπόστολοι προσηγορεύθησαν.
pass_a_gloss: That also having become a man he endured to suffer and be dishonored and will come again with glory, hear the prophecies spoken to this effect. There are these things: 'For which he gave his soul to death and was reckoned with the lawless, he himself bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the lawless. For my servant will understand and will be exalted and glorified exceedingly. Just as many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be dishonored among men and your glory among men, so many nations will marvel and kings will shut their mouths in awe; for those who have not been told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.' 'Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We have told him as a child, as a root in dry ground. He has no form or beauty; and we saw him, and he had no form or beauty, but his appearance was dishonored and lacking among men.' A man in suffering and knowing how to bear weakness, because his face was turned away, he was dishonored and not reckoned. This one bears our sins and suffers on our behalf, and we reckoned him to be in pain and in suffering and in evil. But he was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our sins; the discipline of peace was upon him, by his bruise we were healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, each man has gone astray in his own way; and he gave him over to our sins, and he did not open his mouth because of his affliction. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. After he was crucified and all who knew him denied him, later, having risen from the dead and appeared to them and having encountered the prophecies in which all these things were spoken as going to happen, having taught, and having ascended into heaven, having seen and believed and having received power sent from there by him, they came to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.
pass_b_english: As we reflect on the profound sacrifice of Christ, who became human and endured suffering and dishonor, we are reminded that He will return in glory. Let us consider the prophecies that speak to this very phenomenon (Isaiah 53:3-12). We find a remarkable passage that declares, 'He gave His life to death, and was counted among the wicked, yet He bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the wicked.' The prophecy continues, 'My servant will understand and be exalted, and He will be glorified beyond measure.' It's striking to note that just as many will be astonished at Him, so His appearance will be marred among men, and His glory will be unrecognized - yet many nations will marvel, and kings will be awestruck, for those who have not heard about Him will see, and those who have not been told will understand.

The question is posed, 'Lord, who has believed our message? To whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?' We are told that we presented Him as a child, like a root in dry ground, without form or beauty; and when we saw Him, He had no attractive appearance, but rather a disfigured and unimpressive one. He was a man who suffered and knew weakness, with a face that was disfigured, and He was despised and not esteemed. This is the One who bore our sins and suffered on our behalf, yet we thought He was afflicted, suffering, and evil. However, it was our transgressions that wounded Him, our sins that bruised Him; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His wounds, we are healed.

We have all strayed like sheep, each going our own way, and He gave Himself over to our sins; despite His affliction, He did not open His mouth. Like a sheep led to slaughter, or a lamb before its shearer, He remained silent, not opening His mouth. In His humiliation, His judgment was taken away. After He was crucified, all who knew Him denied Him, but later, having risen from the dead, appeared to them, and encountered the prophecies that foretold these events, He taught them, and as He ascended into heaven, they saw, believed, and received power sent from Him, and they went out to every nation, teaching these things, and were called apostles. The profound impact of Christ's sacrifice and resurrection continues to shape our understanding of God's plan for humanity.

review.notes: Pass B is a paraphrase/commentary rather than a translation. It adds significant introductory and concluding commentary not present in the Greek (e.g., 'As we reflect on the profound sacrifice...', 'The profound impact of Christ's sacrifice...'). It also introduces a false scripture citation: the Greek text contains no citation for Isaiah 53:3-12, but Pass B inserts '(Isaiah 53:3-12)' into the text. Furthermore, Pass B alters the agency/meaning of the Greek in the final section: the Greek says 'having taught [the disciples], and having ascended... they [the disciples] taught these things' (διδάξαντος... ταῦτα ἐδίδαξαν), whereas Pass B says 'He taught them, and as He ascended... they saw... and they went out... teaching these things', which shifts the focus of the teaching action.
reasons: Pass B adds non-existent commentary: 'As we reflect on the profound sacrifice of Christ...' and 'The profound impact of Christ's sacrifice and resurrection continues to shape our understanding of God's plan for humanity.'
Pass B adds a scripture citation '(Isaiah 53:3-12)' not present in the Greek source.
